papers.title: Generic properties of the Laplace spectrum and eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: We prove that the spectrum of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary is generically linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we prove that pointwise products of eigenfunctions generically are linearly independent. The proof is based on conformal perturbations of the metric. The result implies in particular that generically the truncation of the continuous functions on $M$ by spectral projections of the Laplace operator is given by symmetric matrices.

papers.title: IRA Rigidity and boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of Boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras and study their general properties. We show that every Boomerang subalgebra of $L(\Gamma)$ is the group von Neumann algebra of a Boomerang subgroup when $\Gamma$ is a countable $C^*$-simple acylindrically hyperbolic group or a finite product of such groups. Consequently, every such group is invariant random algebra (IRA) rigid: every IRA arises as the pushforward of an invariant random subgroup (IRS) under the group von Neumann algebra construction. We also establish IRA rigidity for adjoint $K$-split higher rank $S$-arithmetic groups, as well as for all countable mixed identity-free (MIF) groups and their finite products. Consequently, IRA rigidity holds for countable groups admitting a topologically free minimal extremely proximal action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points. The same conclusion holds for countable groups admitting a faithful minimal action of general type on a tree whose induced boundary action is topologically free, and for finite products of groups admitting either of these actions.

papers.title: Scaling Limits as Extensions of Continuous Bundles of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We analyze scaling limits in algebraic quantum field theory using continuous bundles of C*-algebras. Different conditions of continuity on such bundles encode different strengths of approximation of the theory by its scaling limit. As a proof of concept, we consider the small-distance scaling limit of the theory of a massive free scalar field, which corresponds to a massless free scalar field. We provide a number of examples of local algebras of observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is merely lower semicontinuous. Further, we construct an algebra of nonlocal observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is uniformly continuous.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).

papers.title: The Quasi-linearity problem for Jordan-Banach algebras: a topological characterization
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{J}$ be a JB$^*$-algebra with no quotients isomorphic to any spin factor. Let $\mu$ be a local quasi-linear Jordan functional on $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$. We show that $\mu$ is a linear functional on $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$ if and only if the restriction of $\mu$ to the closed unit ball of $\mathfrak{J}_{sa}$ is uniformly weakly continuous.

papers.title: The Berry--Esseen estimate in the Boolean central limit theorem
papers.abstract: We estimate the L\'evy distance to the symmetric Bernoulli distribution for normalized Boolean convolution powers of a probability measure with mean zero and variance one. If the absolute moment of order $r$ is finite, we obtain the upper bounds $o(n^{-(r-2)/6})$ for $2<r<5$ and $O(n^{-1/2})$ for $r\ge5$. The proof relies on an inequality that controls the L\'evy distance to the Bernoulli law by the values of the reciprocal Cauchy transform at two points. For each $r\ge2$, we also construct a single fixed distribution whose absolute moments are finite exactly up to order $r$, and show that the exponent $\min\{(r-2)/6,1/2\}$ cannot be improved. Under only a finite second moment assumption, the convergence can be arbitrarily slow.
